RagShortTexts: The standing military of Sclavenians in 374 AD relied upon veteran formations specialized in disciplined field deployment.
Combining heavy protective armor with specialized assault weaponry, the troops executed tactical doctrines honed in frontier engagements.
Commanders emphasized coordinated shock charges and defensive stability, preventing frontline collapse against aggressive cavalry raids.

Variants.Content: The martial renown of Sclavenians rested upon exhaustive drilling and veteran battlefield cohesion during the turbulent close of the 4th century. Core tactical doctrine integrated heavy shield formations with disciplined skirmishing wings, executing tactical maneuvers designed to absorb and counter enemy shock. Along vulnerable sectors, defensive engineers implemented field fortifications and obstacles, breaking the initial momentum of hostile assaults. Once enemy ranks faltered, armored shock reserves counter-charged under thunderous horn blasts, crushing exposed flanks with heavy swords and barbed spears. This balance of resilient endurance and ferocious striking power formed the military bedrock preserving Sclavenians against overwhelming regional adversaries.

The drums beat the advance across the Sclavenian field, and the front rank locks shields with the men beside it. Warhorses slam into the wall, and the rear files thrust spears through each gap before the line can split. A soldier who steps back without the horn order is cut down by his own sergeant, since retreat means instant death in this formation.

From the command tent, the officers study the field with a wax tablet and a row of pins. Victory depends on supply wagons reaching the wings on time and on the infantry holding a straight line. Once the center stands firm, the flanking cavalry can close the trap, and the lord's share of the spoils is counted before the dead are buried.
